Triage: lands in `area:ux` · `domain:server` · `priority:p2` · Feature · `pm:queue` · size M. `area:i18n` is not a North Star area. The p2 grade was set by a person, and it stands.
Rationale: this is a new capability, one refusal naming several declared reasons, each translated. That makes it a Feature. Its purpose is that the person reads every reason in their language, so it sits with the i18n experience work in `area:ux`. It is the refusal-side twin of #36853, which needs a list-shaped keyed param in `service-messaging` for approval notices. The claiming seat should look at both together. objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2759 is blocked by this card.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaacEFVpyQ6C5mcRQs

Decision analysis · 2026-11-25T23:47Z · decision thread for zone o5-U (inbox 7177747783)

## 维护者速读

- 问题：一个动作一次检查多条记录、整体拒绝时要说好几句话（这条已报销、那条未审批……）。现在的拒绝语目录一次只能回一句，所以 HotCRM 的「提交报销」在中文界面下只能给用户看英文清单。
- 选项：A 一次抛出可以带多条已登记的原因，每条按用户语言翻译后逐行回出，约 1 个服务端 PR 加 1 个控制台小 PR；B 只给模板加一个「列表」格式器，同一句话套多个名字可以，不同原因混在一起仍不行；C 平台不改，应用只报第一条问题；D 维持现状，HotCRM 继续英文。
- 推荐 A：拒绝本来就是一组已登记的句子，而不是一句话；用户要看完整清单才知道哪几条要处理。
- 不定会怎样：HotCRM 的报销提交继续英文，hotcrm#2759 持续挂起；后续其它批量动作（批量审批、批量转移）遇到同样的墙。

## Background

Since #34273 (PR #34719) an action may declare a `refusals` catalogue and the server answers a declared code in the caller's locale; since #33214 (PR #33641) an entry may hold several sentences keyed by `reason`, each with `params`. The throw address is one `reason` string and one non-array `params` object (`SandboxRefusalAddress`), and `declaredAnswer` picks exactly one sentence. An all-or-nothing selection check has one sentence per offending record with different reasons, so it cannot be expressed. HotCRM 6.6.0 `crm_expense.submit_for_reimbursement` keeps English literals (hotcrm#2759 blocked on this card). The resolver is shared with hooks (`resolveSandboxedRefusal`, `resolveInProcessHookRefusal`), so any ruling reaches both.

## Governing text

- `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` docblock (ruling 6431311681 letter A): "A hook's refusal catalogue names every refusal its code may throw. The runtime answers a declared code with the declared message in the caller's locale; it refuses a code the catalogue does not declare, loudly." — `grep -n "ruling 6431311681" packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`
- `packages/spec/src/data/declared-entry.zod.ts` `reasons` describe: "Further sentences under this same code, keyed by the snake_case reason the hook throws beside the code ({ code, reason }): { message }. The wire code and status stay this entry's. A reason not declared here is refused loudly." — `grep -n "Further sentences under this same code" packages/spec/src/data/declared-entry.zod.ts`
- ADR-0112 amendment 2026-08-17: `error.code` closed at every door, `declaredCode` the open sibling, `userMessage` the sentence for the person; `ApiErrorSchema.details: z.unknown()` "Additional error context (e.g. field validation errors)" — `grep -n "declaredCode\|details:" packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts`
- NORTH-STAR feature row: "② · The whole application speaks the customer's language … notifications land in the right language too · i18n" — `grep -n "speaks the customer's language" docs/NORTH-STAR.md`

## Protocol

The catalogue entry schema (`message`, `status`, `reasons`, `params`) does not change and no translation key changes. What widens is what a body may throw (the address) and what the wire answer carries. `Metadata-protocol: added` (the body's throw shape is authored metadata; nothing accepted today is refused).

## Premises (each with a re-check)

1. The address reads `reason` only as a non-empty string and `params` only as a non-array object — `sed -n 2683,2700p packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts`
2. `declaredAnswer` renders one sentence per throw — `sed -n 383,413p packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-refusal-catalogue.ts`
3. The template dialect has no list/repeat construct (formatters are scalar) — `sed -n 2270,2282p packages/formula/src/validate.ts`
4. The wire carries `userMessage: string` and `details: unknown`; the console shows a refusal's first sentence with the rest behind "More" — `grep -n "userMessage\|details:" packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts; sed -n 10,20p ui/packages/app-shell/src/components/RefusalMessage.tsx`
5. Twin #36853 is a different layer: `NotificationTextRenderer` resolves a keyed param with `t(key, locale)` and no params — `grep -n "t(key" packages/services/service-messaging/src/notification-text.ts`
6. Both run paths (sandboxed body, in-process handler) answer through one `declaredAnswer` and are pinned byte-identical (PR #33641) — `grep -n "declaredAnswer(" packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-refusal-catalogue.ts`

## The question in one sentence

When an action refuses a whole selection for several different reasons, the person reads either one translated sentence or an English list; nothing lets every reason arrive in their language.

## Options × real cost × workload

| | What | What the person sees | Workload |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | One throw may carry an ordered list of declared reasons, each with its own params, under one declared code: `{ code, reasons: [{ reason, params? }, …] }`. Each reason is checked against the catalogue exactly as a single reason is today (undeclared literal refused at save; undeclared at run ⇒ 500 fault for the whole throw). Each sentence renders translated; `userMessage` is the sentences joined by newline, with the entry's own `message` as the closing line when a list was thrown; `details.refusals: [{ reason, message }]` carries the list structured. Console renders a multi-line `userMessage` as a list. Hooks get it through the shared resolver. | Every line in their language, in the order the body chose; the closing line ("Nothing was submitted.") last. | domain:server 1 PR, size L (runtime address + resolver + spec literal-reason reader + lint + docs + parity tests). Precedent: PR #33641 (+2110/−174, reasons+params+handler path, wider than this); PR #34719 (+2037/−316). Estimate well under either. domain:ui 1 PR, size S (RefusalMessage lines → list), no measured precedent. |
| B | A list formatter in the template (`{{ names \| list }}`) only. | Same sentence over several names translates; different reasons in one answer still cannot. HotCRM's case is not covered. | domain:server 1 PR, size M (formula formatter + i18n list join). No precedent. Does not close the card. |
| C | Platform unchanged; the app refuses on the first offending record only. | One translated sentence; the person fixes one record, resubmits, meets the next. | 0 platform PRs; HotCRM rewrites its action. |
| D | Status quo; the app pre-renders the list into a string param, or keeps English literals. | English lines inside a translated frame, or all English. | 0 PRs; violates the rule that no action composes language; hotcrm#2759 stays blocked. |

Business translation: A = a validation result is a list of findings (as a bulk save returns per-record errors on every mainstream platform); B = a nicer sentence for one kind of problem; C = one problem at a time, more round trips; D = a Chinese UI that speaks English in its most frequent batch action.

## Four axes (business stance)

- **Real business need (②)** — measured: HotCRM 6.6.0 expense submission answers five English lines to a zh-CN user; hotcrm#2759 is blocked on this card; the same downstream app already moved 83 hook refusals and two action refusals into catalogues (#34273 body). Every batch action (bulk approve, bulk reassign, bulk close) has the same shape, so this is a class, not one screen.
- **Long-term fit (①)** — a refusal is a set of declared sentences, not one. Two years out, the platform's refusal answer reads: one declared code, an ordered list of declared reasons each in the person's language, structured on the wire so an agent (MCP) and the console can both list them; this is how bulk DML results and RFC 9457 problem-detail `errors[]` are modelled elsewhere. A is an array of what already exists (declared reasons + params), under the existing `details` channel; B invents a second expressive channel inside sentences; C/D leave a hole every batch action falls into.
- **AI-error-proofing (③)** — with A every sentence stays in the catalogue: an AI that writes an undeclared reason meets a publish refusal (literal) or a loud 500 (computed); the person never sees untranslated prose. With D the AI's natural move is `params: { lines: '…English…' }` and the English ships silently inside a translated frame. With B/C the AI keeps writing `throw new Error(list)`. A is the loud option.
- **Startup focus (④)** — A adds no catalogue key, no translation key, no gate, no new formatter grammar; it widens one throw shape and one wire field that already exists (`details`). B adds grammar that does not close the case.

os-decision-facets
① Long-term fit: A reuses declared reasons/params and the existing `details` channel; no new concept, one shape widened (list of what exists).
② Business pull: HotCRM 6.6.0 expense submit, hotcrm#2759 blocked; every all-or-nothing batch action has the same shape.
③ AI-error-proofing: every line stays catalogue-declared, undeclared ⇒ save refusal / loud 500; the alternative is English inside a translated frame, silently.
④ Startup focus: no new key, no new translation key, no gate; B would add template grammar without closing the card.
Prior rulings read: refusal · refusals · 36853 · multi-reason → 0 hits in coordinator/rulings.md and decisions/待决汇总.md; ADR-0112 amendment (declaredCode/userMessage) read; rulings 6431311681 A and 6879477573 A read in hook.zod.ts; thread: none.

## Recommendation: A

Self-check: 只看①选 A;②③④ 是否翻转:否。

Confidence gaps: (a) hotcrm's action source is not in this container; the five lines are taken from the card's probe table on 18.6.0. (b) The console half (list rendering) has no measured precedent; it is a small change to `RefusalMessage`. (c) Whether MCP's refusal envelope relays `details` is not re-measured here; the dev checks it on claim.

Not taken: B does not cover different reasons in one answer; C trades the list the person relies on for round trips; D breaks the one rule that makes translation possible.

## Twin #36853

Different layer (notification text, `service-messaging` keyed params), different card (Bug, pm:queue, Blocked-by #36846). It stays its own card. Shared only in principle: both join a list per locale; if the dev of either finds a reusable per-locale list join in `@objectstack/spec` i18n helpers, both use it. Not a requirement of this ruling.

## Execution after the ruling (A)

1. Zone o5-U claims #36877 (`domain:server`, size L, `mode:subagent` or thread by the runbook). Dispatch premise: the dev re-runs premises 1–6 first; a failed premise reports a fork.
2. Server PR: (a) the sandbox address accepts `reasons: [{ reason, params? }]` beside the existing `reason`/`params` form; both on one throw ⇒ fault; (b) `declaredAnswer` checks every listed reason against the entry; one undeclared ⇒ the whole throw is the loud fault, naming the reason; (c) each sentence renders translated and param-filled as today; `userMessage` = lines joined by `\n`, the entry's `message` appended as the last line only when a list was thrown; `details.refusals: [{ reason, message }]`; (d) the spec literal reader (`hookRefusalReasonsThrownIn` and the action twin) reads reasons inside an array literal too; lint unchanged otherwise; (e) parity pin: sandboxed body and in-process handler answer byte-identical for a list throw (PR #33641 pattern); (f) `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Skills-docs:` follow-up for `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md` and `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md`.
3. UI follow-up card under #36877 (`domain:ui`, size S): `RefusalMessage` renders a multi-line `userMessage` as a list in the same alert box (first line no longer hides the rest behind "More").
4. hotcrm#2759 unblocks on the release that carries the server PR.
